prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on the balance sheet: profit covers interest costs 10.5 times over. Also in its favour: debt is lower than shareholders' equity (debt-to-equity 0.25); return on capital employed is 34.5%, a strong return on the money in the business; and profit grew 394.6% a year on average over three years. Other areas on this side: cash flow and the balance sheet, what the price asks for the earnings, growth.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on growth: profit fell 100% compared with a year earlier. Also against it: the share price is 28% below its 52-week high; free cash flow for the last financial year was negative: the business spent more than it generated; and one-year volatility is 50.1%, high. Other areas on this side: the recent price trend, cash flow and the balance sheet, price behaviour.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 7 points in favour and 4 against give more points in favour. The pool score is 66 of 100. The side that carries most weight is the balance sheet. That gives an educational rating of Overweight with low confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
